transcript.text: Good evening everyone. We've got the Alpha furnace campaign scheduled for tonight, with Beta available as an alternate. Before I authorize anything, I need to hear from process engineering and EHS on their final checks. I also want to make sure we're comfortable with our nitrogen situation — we have 1,000 normal cubic meters available before the next delivery, which isn't expected until after tomorrow's day shift. Whoever needs to weigh in, go ahead.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue. My validated process calculation, which I completed this morning but haven't yet entered in the production plan, shows that the Alpha campaign requires exactly 1,200 normal cubic meters of nitrogen, while the Beta campaign requires exactly 600 normal cubic meters. With only 1,000 normal cubic meters available before the next delivery, Alpha would come up 200 short. Beta, on the other hand, can be completed within our available supply.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an EHS issue with the Beta furnace. My review of the area records found that the oxygen monitor serving the Beta furnace is overdue for calibration. The approved calibration procedure takes exactly 2 hours before Beta can start, and the calibration-register synchronization is still pending. So if we go with Beta, we need to account for that 2-hour calibration delay before startup.
